body.statement: For every fixed source exponent \(s>0\) and every nondegenerate model class containing a constant-contrast two-outcome submodel with \(a_0>0\), \(\delta_{n,e}^\star\asymp n^{-1/2}\). The upper bound is attained by the bounded oracle estimator \(\widehat\Psi_e\), and the lower bound holds by a one-dimensional regular submodel in the constant Fourier coordinate. Thus covariance eigen-decay cannot improve the worst-case oracle exponent under RKHS-norm separation.
body.justification: This identifies the correct oracle benchmark before nuisance and spectral effects are compared.
body.gap: Direct spectral tests obtain nonparametric rates in a stronger \(L^2\)-type separation, while Jain and Luedtke do not state the all-tests RKHS-norm radius.
body.consumer: It prevents the 401(k) analysis from interpreting whitening as an exponent improvement that the chosen estimand cannot support.
